findings.description: `ln -s "$(git cat-file blob "$oid")" "$dest"` takes the PR-committed link target as an argument with no `--`. A link whose target starts with `-` is read as `ln` options. The step can then create, or with `-f` overwrite, a symlink outside `.claude-pr-agents/` (in the repo root or any runner-writable directory). That breaks the step's own guarantee that nothing is written outside the snapshot directory.
findings.body:
The snapshot loop passes the PR-controlled symlink target to `ln` with no `--` in front of it. Git stores any bytes as a link's target, so a PR can commit something like `.agents/x/AGENTS.md` as a link whose target is `-f`. The loop then runs:

```sh
ln -s -f .claude-pr-agents/.agents/x/AGENTS.md
```

GNU `ln` given one operand creates `./AGENTS.md` in the workspace root. That replaces, with a dangling link, the `AGENTS.md` that the first `RESTORE_PATHS` pass (`AGENTS.md .agents`) just restored from the merge base. No later step restores it, so the review runs without the base's instructions that `CLAUDE.md` imports.

A clustered `-ft<dir>` or `--target-directory=<dir>` places or overwrites a link in any directory the runner can write to, including the action's checkout under `_actions/`. The link always points at `.claude-pr-agents/<path>`, which `ln` never wrote, so the PR can't inject content this way. It can still delete or replace files outside the snapshot, which is the guarantee the step's comment (L166-L171) and the CHANGELOG entry state.

None of the new restore tests uses a link target that starts with `-`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/0e930ee890bf0350f0ceefb81c395e1433010c2a/templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#L191

Fix: end option parsing before the target, in this template and in the rendered `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml:213`, which `test/workflow-sync.test.ts` keeps in sync. A test committing a link with target `-f` would pin it.

findings.description: The rendered copy of the workflow has the same `ln -s` without `--` as the template, so a PR link target starting with `-` is parsed as `ln` options and can write a symlink outside `.claude-pr-agents/`, e.g. over the restored root `AGENTS.md`.
findings.body:
This is the same defect as `templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml:191`, in this repository's rendered workflow. `RESTORE_PATHS` here is `AGENTS.md .agents templates`, so a link target of `-f` under `.agents/` or `templates/` named `AGENTS.md` replaces the merge-base `AGENTS.md` restored in the first pass with a dangling link. `-ft<dir>` writes into any directory the runner can write to.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/0e930ee890bf0350f0ceefb81c395e1433010c2a/.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#L213

Apply the same `--` fix as in the template; `test/workflow-sync.test.ts` requires the two copies to match.

findings.description: Adding `/.claude-pr-agents/` to `.git/info/exclude` also hides the snapshot from ripgrep-backed Grep/Glob, so reviewers can reach the PR's copies only by explicit-path Read; the skill could say so.
The snapshot loop's `case` silently skips gitlinks (160000) and any other mode. Skipping is the safe choice, but it is untested and unstated; a one-line why-comment would help.

`$(git cat-file blob "$oid")` strips trailing newlines from a link target, so a pathological target ending in a newline isn't reproduced byte for byte. There is no consequence for a read-only snapshot.
The edited decision 21 paragraph wasn't rewrapped: a line breaks short after "a repository whose". Reflow it to the file's width.
The symlink `it.each` case picks the link target by `link.endsWith(".md")`, which hides the file-link and directory-link scenarios inside one body. Put the target kind in the table row instead.
